clue.text: Quick to bracket old taxmen as thieving

indicators.note: to bracket something is to enclose it, so the word for quick goes round the taxmen

parts.note: pacy means quick, fast-moving
IR is Inland Revenue, the former UK tax authority, now merged into HMRC

explanation.surface: Someone says the old tax inspectors were quick to be called thieves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bracket' is the container signal. The Inland Revenue was Britain's tax collector until 2005, hence 'old taxmen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken as a noun, thieving is stealing, and robbery at sea or copying without permission are both called this.

indicators.note: entertaining guests means having them in, so the seaside word holds the group

parts.note: a pier is a structure jutting into the sea at a resort
REM is a well-known American rock band

explanation.surface: A seaside pier is laying on a show for a band's frontman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' is the container signal. A pier is a typical feature of a British seaside resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime minister is called this, a head of government and so the top political leader.

parts.note: Roy and Al are two boys' names
the second of the two names, Al

explanation.surface: Two boys must be split up when they keep asking for things.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is ASKING; split into two words it reads AS KING, and to behave as a king is to be regal.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting like a monarch is being kingly or regal, the sense the split cross-reference gives.

clue.text: Man cheated on topless bird, in biting

indicators.note: in places the shortened bird within the word for biting

parts.note: a biting wind is a cold one

indicators.note: topless says the bird loses its top letter

parts.note: a duck is a water bird

explanation.surface: A man who was betrayed watches a bird with its top missing in a bitter wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' leaves UCK; 'in' is the container signal. 'Bird' tempts with CUCKOO, but no reading of the clue builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband whose wife is unfaithful is traditionally given this old word.

indicators.note: a design of something rearranges it into a new pattern, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the answer to 11 across is RIALTO

explanation.surface: A design taken from a Venetian bridge is put to use in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Design of' rearranges RIALTO, the answer at 11.
explanation.definitionFit: To fashion something is to shape or adapt it, as a cutter adjusts clothes to fit, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Shocked to see old ovens retaining hot temperature

indicators.note: retaining means keeping something inside, so the ovens hold the letter for hot

parts.note: Agas are traditional British cast-iron range cookers
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled that the old ovens keep the temperature so hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retaining' puts H inside AGAS, then T follows. An AGA is a heavy British range cooker that stays hot all the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Being horrified or amazed is a synonym of being shocked.

clue.text: Resort where priests seen holding drinks up

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the priests go round the reversed drinks

parts.note: lamas are Tibetan Buddhist priests

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says this word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: laps means drinks, as a cat laps milk

explanation.surface: A holiday resort where priests can be seen with drinks raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives SPAL in this down clue; 'holding' is the container signal. Las Palmas is on Gran Canaria.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canary Islands city is a popular holiday destination, an example of a resort.

indicators.note: in places the nickel symbol within the word for a cold

parts.note: rheum is watery discharge from a head cold, and can mean the cold itself
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

explanation.surface: A chemist notes nickel turns up in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. Rheum is an old word for the running nose of a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhenium is a rare metallic chemical element, number 75, an example of an element.

clue.text: Don't hold back having got cut — gash the swine!

parts.note: taken as written
to hew is to cut, as with an axe
a gash is a hole or rent
a hog is a pig, a swine

explanation.surface: An urgent cry to slash the pig with no restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got cut' looks like one shortened word, but GOT stays whole and 'cut' is HEW.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to do something fully without restraint, so it fits not holding back.

definitions.meaning: ..., as an adverb of degree, means so, as in 'so good'
as an adjective it means precise

explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it intensifies like so, and as an adjective it means precisely this one.

clue.text: Stage performer taking lace finally through shoe fastener

indicators.note: through says these letters run inside the shoe word

parts.note: a clog is a wooden-soled shoe
a thesp is an informal word for an actor

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word lace

explanation.surface: An actor threads a lace through a shoe's fastening at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives E, the last letter of lace; 'through' is the container signal, and 'taking' just joins actor and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The wooden clip that holds washing on a line is a kind of fastener.

parts.note: the rial is the currency of Iran and other countries
taken as written

explanation.surface: Money is carried over to a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rialto is the famous bridge over the Grand Canal in Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: This Venetian structure over the Grand Canal is a famous example of a bridge.

parts.note: his is the male counterpart of her
panic is the opposite of composure

explanation.surface: She stays calm, but he loses his head.
explanation.walkthrough: One of several 'but ___' clues: fill the gap with the opposite of each word of the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone of Spanish-speaking descent from Latin America is described by this word.

parts.note: a break is a lucky chance, an opportunity
down means dispirited or discouraged

explanation.surface: A chance was missed and the person felt let down.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapse or malfunction, of a car or of health, is a failure.

indicators.note: being disorganised says the letters of lamenting are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the organisation is in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being disorganised' rearranges LAMENTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranging things in order or in line is an organisation of them, a near synonym.

parts.note: I'm is the first-person counterpart of you're
AM, morning, is the opposite of PM, afternoon

explanation.surface: You may be the Prime Minister, but I outrank you as a cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: Another 'but ___' clue: swap each part for its opposite, I'M for YOU'RE and AM for PM.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who leads prayers in a mosque is a Muslim religious leader.

definitions.meaning: to work as a waiter at table

explanation.definitionFit: As a command it asks someone to stay, and it also means attend tables in a restaurant.

parts.note: win is the opposite of lose
some is the lesser counterpart of many, as in the saying

explanation.surface: You lose many, but you win some, which is only fair.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'but ___' clue on the saying 'you win some, you lose some'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming and attractive in looks, as fair can mean beautiful, is a synonym.

indicators.note: becoming says the letters turn into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A woman's companion is turning into her escort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' rearranges HER ESCORT. Jane Eyre, in Charlotte Bronte's novel, marries Mr Rochester.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Rochester is the man Jane Eyre loves in the novel, so he is Jane's man.

clue.text: At school, not using head, so in work

indicators.note: not using head says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: learning is what you are doing at school

explanation.surface: A pupil who skips thinking is supposedly working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not using head' removes L from LEARNING.
explanation.definitionFit: Being paid for a job is being in work, so the participle stands for employed.

definitions.meaning: to bang is to strike hard
the tool shown with the sickle on the Soviet flag

explanation.definitionFit: To bang is to strike repeatedly, and the tool crossed with a sickle appears on the Soviet flag.

clue.text: You monk, but ___ (time to get fully immersed)

parts.note: I is the first-person counterpart of you
a nun is the female counterpart of a monk
a date is a point in time

explanation.surface: You may be a monk, but I am a nun, so I plunge in.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'but ___' clue: swap you for I and monk for nun, then add DATE for 'time'.
explanation.definitionFit: To flood or overwhelm is to submerge, making something fully immersed in water.

indicators.note: say signals how a word is spoken, here with an Australian accent

parts.note: cricketers are players, said in an Aussie accent

explanation.surface: A gadget is chosen for the Australian cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: An Australian accent turns the vowel of the word for cricketers into something near PLIERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pincers for gripping and bending wire are a common hand tool.

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's is a link meaning has

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to breaking a piece of Japanese china.
explanation.definitionFit: This brightly decorated ware from Arita in Japan is a kind of porcelain.

clue.text: Understood to go before M — 007, was he?

parts.note: roger is radio talk for message received and understood
the double zero looks like two letter Os
the 7 is the answer at 7-down, rhenium, whose symbol is Re

explanation.surface: In a Bond film, the agent says he understands before going to see his boss M.
explanation.walkthrough: The 7 in 007 refers to 7-down, RHENIUM, chemical symbol RE. M is the head of the secret service in Bond films.
explanation.definitionFit: He played James Bond, agent 007, in seven films from 1973 to 1985.

definitions.meaning: in fact, as a matter of fact

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in fact, and a broadcast shown at the moment of events is live.

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: cut says the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: a torte is a rich layered cake

explanation.surface: Someone is upset that the old cake has been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims the final E from TORTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleed someone is to drain them of money, the same as to wring it from them by force.

clue.text: Demanding covering, every cloud thus covered?

indicators.note: thus covered says, in the way the cloud is lined, the covering sits inside

parts.note: every cloud has a silver lining, and Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
skin is a covering

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether every cloud has its covering.
explanation.walkthrough: Silver is not printed: the proverb 'every cloud has a silver lining' supplies it, and 'thus covered' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking for something is requesting it, close in sense to demanding it.
